newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli unions to vote on labour dispute.
newsitem.headline: Israeli unions to vote on labour dispute.

text.p: Israeli unions will vote on Sunday whether to declare a labour dispute which could lead to a general strike, a labour leader said on Thursday.

Histadrut labour federation secretary-general Amir Peretz made the announcement after meeting with Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman in an attempt to reach a compromise on a controversial package of economic reforms.
The two failed to reach any agreement, and are due to meet again Sunday evening.

Thursday's meeting followed cabinet approval on Wednesday night of 100 structural reforms as part of an effort to revive Israel's flagging economic growth. The reforms include privatisation, capital market and foreign currency reforms, and sectoral deregulation.
At the same meeting, the cabinet also approved a Treasury plan to cut 2.3 billion shekels from 1998's planned 164.4 billion shekel budget and set next year's inflation target at seven to 10 percent.
"I think the programme to increase competition is a programme for increasing unemployment in Israel, attacking workers' rights in almost every sector," Peretz told reporters before the meeting.
He vowed to fight the reforms but stopped short of threatening a general strike, saying "this is a possibility at some future date."
Responding, Neeman said "there is no need for fears from the work force. Growth will bring more jobs."
Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel, meanwhile, criticised the new inflation target.
"Fixing the target at this level, which is identical to the 1997 target, does not reflect sufficient progress towards reducing inflation," Frenkel said in a statement.
He expressed support for the structural changes and the cabinet's decision to keep the budget deficit ceiling at 2.4 percent of gross domestic product as originally targeted.
Frenkel had reportedly been urging the government to reduce next year's inflation target to six to nine percent.
